Chrzanow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chrzanów, Poland

Demolished. Before establishing their own cemetery, Chrzanów's earliest Jewish settlers (documented from at least 1590, with an independent community from 1745) buried their dead in nearby Olkusz. This 'small' original cemetery was founded in 1759 and expanded several times, remaining in use into the early 19th century. By 1880, Jews made up 59% of Chrzanów's population, and Jewish councilmembers held a decisive council majority from 1888-1920, including Jewish mayor Dr. Zygmunt Keppler until 1912. During WWII, Germans extended Podwale Street through part of this cemetery, relocating remains to Chrzanów's newer cemetery and using tombstones for construction; a petrol station now occupies part of the original grounds.
